open_points.subject: start_instance
open_points.text: start_instance: [ORCHESTRATION] Once every listener is open it MUST accept connections on each and serve every connection on a thread of its own, so that a request waiting for a lock holds no other: a request on the service API's listener MUST be read into an HttpRequest, every field of = models.HttpRequest taken from its request line and header fields, each header field's value its bytes decoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant with every byte that is not part of a valid sequence replaced by the imported TEXT_REPLACEMENT_CHARACTER constant, a request line or header block it cannot read ending the connection without an answer, and handed to serve_service_request with its body read whole as bytes, an empty body when it declares none; a request on the owner interface's listener MUST be read into an HttpRequest the same way and handed to serve_owner_request with the connection's body stream unread, a stream that ends at the request's declared length or, for a body framed in chunks, gives the decoded bytes as they are read; the HttpResponse either answers MUST be written back as one response with its status and body unchanged and its header fields, each unchanged and in its order, followed by one more, the field the imported CONTENT_LENGTH_HEADER constant names giving the body's length in bytes, which neither surface's answer holds since writing it is this listener's alone, so that a client knows where the answer ends while the connection stays open.
open_points.other_text:
def serve_owner_request(request: HttpRequest, body: ByteStream) -> HttpResponse
def serve_service_request(request: HttpRequest, body: bytes) -> HttpResponse
open_points.question: Either the contracts of serve_owner_request and serve_service_request must guarantee that their returned HttpResponse headers never contain the field named by CONTENT_LENGTH_HEADER, or the start_instance note must stop assuming that absence and specify how to handle an already-present field.
